overview.title: AI CODE MOVIE STUDIO in short

blocks.html:
AI CODE MOVIE STUDIO takes a script and reference material and has Gemini build video code that runs on HTML Canvas and the Web Audio API. It runs inside Google’s Gemini Canvas, so there is nothing to install and no API key to supply.

You can preview the result on the spot and take it away either as MP4 / WebM or as the code that draws the video. That makes it a quick way to rough out the opening and ending videos of a SlideCast Studio project.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Worth saying up front
blocks.text: Generation is a lottery. Sometimes it lands; sometimes you get “the structure is fine but the treatment is not quite there”. This is not a magic box that produces a finished video in one shot — it is a way to get one draft out quickly.

blocks.html: The audio side is handled by its sibling app, AI CODE BGM STUDIO. Combining the two is the fast way to line up picture and sound. SlideCast Studio itself is covered in the official manual.

blocks.title: 🇯🇵 The app’s interface is in Japanese
blocks.text: AI CODE MOVIE STUDIO ships with a Japanese UI, so the screenshots on this page are Japanese. Each field is spelled out in English below, and the script box accepts English text.

sections.title: What the app does
sections.intro: Write the script, press generate, and a short video plays right there.

blocks.html:
You want a short intro film, a mood piece, or an announcement video — but opening an editor and building it from nothing is heavy. Work out the structure, work out the motion, tidy the frame, add sound if it needs it. This app takes that first step for you.

The uses it is aimed at:

items: Opening and ending sequences for YouTube
Service introduction videos
Mood pieces that establish a world
Announcement videos built around on-screen text
Abstract visual material with motion

blocks.html: If the settings feel like a chore, leave them on おまかせ (auto). Writing only the script, generating one take and refining from there is often faster.

blocks.title: 🖼️ You can supply image assets
blocks.text: Drop in a logo, a product shot, a key visual, a background or a diagram, and tag each one with its role (logo / product / background / opening / ending / diagram). They are not just references — the actual files appear in the video.

sections.title: Content references and style references
sections.intro: Keeping these two apart is what the app is really good at.

before.label: Content reference
before.text: Script, product copy, structure notes, factual material — what goes into the video.

after.label: Style reference
after.text: Colour, texture, pacing, atmosphere — how the video should feel.

blocks.html:
Because they are separate, you can say “base the content on this document, but take the look from that other reference”. Text, images, PDFs and URLs all work in either slot.

“Analyse and fill in the details” pushes what it finds into the theme and palette fields. References are abstracted rather than copied wholesale.

blocks.text: Undo and redo take you back to the previous result, so you can afford to ask for something drastic and simply step back if it overshoots.

sections.title: Setting expectations honestly
sections.intro: What it is good at, and what it is not.

blocks.html:
This app is not a magic box either. Generation is a lottery: sometimes it lands, sometimes you get “close in feel, but it still needs work”. That comes from Gemini generating code, and from what HTML Canvas can draw, what the Web Audio API can play, what a browser can run, and how stable generated code is.

And frankly, asking any AI service “make me a video as code only, and let me download it” gets you something similar. The idea is not exotic. What is tedious in practice is writing the prompt every time, pasting the code, checking the output, issuing corrections, and rigging up a download. This app is that loop, packaged so you do not repeat it.

before.label: Not what it is for
before.text: Producing a finished video in one shot, or footage you can deliver as-is.
